site.title: PlacementScope
site.purpose: Placements at IIT Guwahati run on rumours, forwards and half-true stories. This guide is built from real interviews with seniors who were placed or went on to further studies.
site.event: Sahyog'26 · Students' Welfare Board × Academic Initiatives Club, IIT Guwahati

domains.name: Electrical & Electronics Core
domains.summary: Analog, digital and signals fundamentals, project-driven interviews, and a research track for those drawn to R&D.

paragraphs: This section covers two paths: core electronics placements on campus, and higher studies leading to research roles.
Technical rounds start with basic fundamentals and quickly move into specialised topics drawn from the projects on your resume.
keyPoints: Standard Analog, Digital and Signals & Systems courses cover 90–95% of Texas Instruments' test and interview syllabus.
NVIDIA expects digital electronics well beyond the college course.
Projects, especially the BTP, steer most technical interviews.

tracks.title: Core placements
points: Primarily open to EEE and ECE students; Texas Instruments also recruits EP and CSE students for embedded roles.
For non-circuital branches, on-campus eligibility is nearly zero. Build a strong CV through hands-on projects, join the Electronics Club, and apply off-campus.
Power electronics and other specialisations need self-study beyond college courses.

tracks.title: Research scope
points: Higher studies let you explore specialised domains and work on advanced research problems; industry roles build practical technical expertise.
After B.Tech or M.Tech, opportunities tend to be design-oriented and technical implementation roles.
PhD graduates can move into senior R&D positions: leading research teams and driving technological development.
Limitation: the research-track senior had not sat campus placements and had only recently started the PhD, so could not compare industry projects with doctoral research.

timeline.detail: For Texas Instruments, standard Analog, Digital and Signals & Systems coursework covers 90–95% of the syllabus.

domains.name: Civil Core
domains.summary: GATE-level fundamentals, form-driven shortlisting, and a decisive HR round with a psychologist on the panel.

paragraphs: This section collects placement experience and practical guidance from recent seniors who went through Civil Engineering core campus recruitment.
Core technical rounds and online screening tests closely follow the pattern and weightage of GATE and IES (Engineering Services Examination), so GATE-level preparation is the benchmark.
keyPoints: Prepare core subjects to GATE standard.
Be ready to defend every line of Forms A, B and C.
The HR round plays a decisive role in final selection.

timeline.detail: Structured company CV forms submitted via Google Forms over a 7–10 day window.
Based on CPI and student category. Interview invitations arrive within 1–2 days.
Some companies (e.g. Spectrum Techno Consultant) run an online test open to most shortlisted candidates (14 of 17 in one case). Questions resemble 1-mark GATE questions.
Early-morning pre-placement presentation, then mandatory document verification (Class 10 & 12 marksheets, category certificates).
15–30 minutes with a panel of 6–7 interviewers covering fundamentals and core sub-disciplines.
Candidates who clear the technical round fill Form C immediately.
30–40 minutes, typically with a professional psychologist and two HR representatives. The day usually runs until about 3:00 PM.

interviewQuestions.q: How many types of foundations are there?
What is the defining depth of a deep foundation?
What traffic facility do you use where multiple roads connect?
Draw the complete stress–strain curve for steel.
Draw the SFD, BMD and deflection curve for a given frame or beam.
Form C: describe a major achievement, a time outside your comfort zone, or a key group project.

general: Shortlisting considers CPI and student category.
Category certificates and Class 10 & 12 marksheets are verified on drive day.

domains.name: Mechanical Core
domains.summary: Core companies want to hire more people than they do. CPI, sincere projects and clear technical delivery are what convert.

paragraphs: This section compiles advice and placement strategy shared by Mechanical Engineering alumni, covering job availability, preparation milestones, software and project choice.
Getting shortlisted is only half the battle; presenting technical concepts clearly converts interview calls into offers.
keyPoints: CPI and solid projects are the two primary factors for core Mechanical placements.
Fusion 360 is enough to start with CAD; ANSYS / Ansys Discovery for simulation.
An Inter-IIT podium is the "cherry on the cake".

general: Seniors name CPI and projects as the two deciding factors for core Mechanical shortlisting. No company-specific cutoffs were recorded.

skills.name: CAD: Fusion 360
skills.detail: Essential and sufficient to start; needed for Kinematics and Design of Machine Elements (DOME). Other tools are easy once fluent.

skills.name: FEA & simulation: ANSYS / Ansys Discovery
skills.detail: Widely used in industrial design roles; licences can be requested through department professors.

skills.name: Practical fabrication
skills.detail: 3D print at least a few physical models to understand real prototyping constraints.

skills.name: Hardware + basic programming/controls
skills.detail: Problem statements that combine fabrication with controls stand out.

skills.name: Technical communication
skills.detail: Explaining design decisions with full reasoning, linking theory to prototypes.

domains.name: Civil Services
domains.summary: Choosing UPSC over placements: retention-heavy preparation, nearly two years of effort, and the value of PORs for the Personality Test.

paragraphs: This section is based on a senior preparing for the UPSC Civil Services Examination, covering the preparation approach, how an engineering background helps, extracurricular involvement and advice for juniors.
For this senior, Civil Services was the primary goal from school onwards; IIT was chosen for exposure and a broad education rather than as a route to campus placements.
keyPoints: UPSC rewards extensive retention more than JEE-style application.
Plan for close to two years of preparation from scratch.
PORs and clubs build examples useful in the Personality Test.

domains.name: Data Science
domains.summary: Statistics, ML, SQL and DSA foundations; 2–3 deep end-to-end projects; and the ability to articulate every trade-off.

paragraphs: This section aggregates preparation insights, project advice and interview strategy shared by a senior alumnus.
Most candidates who miss offers don't lack knowledge; they can't clearly articulate their model choices, metric selection and trade-offs.
keyPoints: Foundations (Statistics, ML, DSA, SQL) matter more than superficial projects.
Recruiters prefer 2–3 well-understood end-to-end projects over many clones.
Expect every project assumption to be cross-examined.

timeline.detail: Typically a mix of DSA coding, complex SQL queries and MCQs on probability, statistics and ML algorithms.
Deep-dive project probing plus live problem solving on the whiteboard.
Growth potential, collaboration and adaptability.

interviewQuestions.q: How did you handle missing data in your project?
How did you mitigate class imbalance?
Why F1-score rather than precision–recall (or vice versa) for your evaluation?
Why XGBoost over a neural network (or a simpler baseline)?
Explain Gradient Boosting or an attention mechanism to a non-technical stakeholder.
Describe a disagreement on technical approach in a team project and how you handled it.

skills.name: Machine Learning & Deep Learning
skills.detail: Regression, trees, boosting, clustering; neural networks; NLP or CV basics depending on role.

skills.name: Mathematics & Statistics
skills.detail: Hypothesis testing, distributions, Bayes' theorem, linear algebra (PCA, SVD), A/B testing.

skills.name: Data engineering & querying
skills.detail: Advanced SQL (window functions, joins, aggregations), Pandas, NumPy, preprocessing pipelines.

skills.name: Coding & problem solving
skills.detail: Standard DSA in Python or C++ for coding screens.

roadmap.title: Master the fundamentals
actions: Probability, statistics, linear algebra, Python, SQL and core ML algorithms.
roadmap.outcome: Theoretical rigour and coding proficiency for tests.

roadmap.title: Build end-to-end projects
actions: Work on real-world datasets (Kaggle, research or industry).
Build complete pipelines: collection, cleaning, EDA, training, tuning, evaluation.
roadmap.outcome: Evidence of deployment, feature engineering and evaluation depth.

roadmap.title: Frame your resume
actions: Write bullets around methodology, tools and quantified metrics.
roadmap.outcome: A CV that survives automated screening and technical questioning.

roadmap.title: Sharpen for the drive

roadmap.outcome: Speed, clarity and confidence in screening tests and technical rounds.

practical.title: End-to-end pipeline ownership
practical.detail: Data collection and cleaning, EDA, model training, hyperparameter tuning and metric evaluation.

practical.title: Problem statement clarity
practical.detail: State the real-world use, and why your model beat simpler baselines.

practical.title: Metrics-driven bullets
practical.detail: e.g. "Improved AUC-ROC from 0.78 to 0.89 using custom feature engineering and hyperparameter tuning."

practical.title: Keep learning visibly
practical.detail: Follow recent papers, open-source tools and competitive data science platforms, and talk about them.

myths.myth: More projects make a stronger resume.
myths.reality: 2–3 well-understood end-to-end projects beat a long list of textbook clones.

myths.myth: People miss offers because they don't know enough.
myths.reality: Most fail because they can't articulate model choices, metrics and trade-offs.

advice.quote: A solid foundation in Statistics, ML, DSA and SQL is far more important than superficial projects.

market.title: Articulation decides

paragraphs: Quantitative finance and high-frequency trading (HFT) combine mathematics, probability, programming and financial concepts to build algorithms and systems used in markets.

keyPoints: Coding and mathematical aptitude carry equal weight.
